memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Amalekites came and attacked the Israelites at Rephidim." - Ex 17:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One short sentence, and everything changes. The water crisis is barely resolved
and an army arrives.

Deuteronomy 25:18 tells us how Amalek fought: they attacked the stragglers at
the rear, "all who were lagging behind," when Israel was weary and worn out.
They targeted the weakest people at the worst moment. That detail explains much
of God's later severity toward them.

Notice the timing. This attack comes immediately after a spiritual low point.
Israel had just questioned whether God was among them, and now they face their
first battle.

We should be careful not to build a formula out of this. It is not a rule that
every spiritual struggle is followed by attack, and reading life that way can
make people anxious and superstitious. But Scripture is honest that difficulties
often arrive in clusters, and that the weary are especially vulnerable.

Peter writes soberly that our enemy "prowls around like a roaring lion looking
for someone to devour" (1 Pet 5:8). He does not say this to frighten us but to
make us alert. And he says it right after telling us to cast our anxiety on God.

Alertness and trust belong together. Watch, and do not be afraid.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When are you most vulnerable, and do you know it about yourself?
2. Who around you is lagging behind and needs protecting?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, make me alert without making me fearful. Help me to watch out for those
who are struggling to keep up. Amen.
